subject: community-medicine
title: Gross and Net Reproduction Rates, SRS, and the Population Pyramid

steps.title: Gross reproduction rate
steps.tx: Daughters only, because daughters become the next mothers: the **gross reproduction rate** averages the number of daughters a newborn girl would bear in her lifetime if she survived all reproductive years at current age specific rates. It equals the total fertility rate multiplied by the proportion of female births (about zero point four eight eight). Mortality is ignored, which the net rate then corrects.
steps.say: Gross reproduction rate counts daughters per woman assuming nobody dies. Multiply total fertility by the female share of births to get it.

steps.title: Net reproduction rate as replacement index
steps.tx: Adjusting the gross rate for deaths of girls and women before and during reproductive life gives the **net reproduction rate**, the true replacement index of demography. A value of one means each woman exactly replaces herself with one surviving daughter; above one the population grows across generations, below one it shrinks. India's net rate hovers near one, consistent with fertility at replacement.
steps.say: Net reproduction rate of one means exact replacement. It asks whether today's mothers leave behind one surviving daughter each.

steps.title: Sample Registration System design
steps.tx: India's **Sample Registration System** runs continuous dual recording in sampled villages and urban blocks: a local recorder lists every birth and death, and an independent supervisor re enumerates each half year, with unmatched events field verified. This dual record system yields annual birth, death, infant mortality, and fertility rates for states, filling the decade long silence between two censuses.
steps.say: The Sample Registration System records vital events twice through two independent channels. Matching the lists produces India's annual birth and death rates.

steps.title: Anatomy of the population pyramid
steps.tx: Stacked horizontal bars of males and females by five year age groups form the **population pyramid**, whose silhouette diagnoses demographic stage at a glance: a broad based triangle means high fertility, a barrel means stationary numbers, and a top heavy urn means decline. India's pyramid shows a narrowing base under a still wide childhood trunk, the portrait of fertility transition in progress.
steps.say: Pyramid shape tells the story: triangle for growth, barrel for stability, urn for decline. India's base is narrowing as fertility falls.

rows: High births, many children, rapid growth

steps.tx: Horizontal bars stacked by sex and by five year age groups draw India's 2011 **population pyramid**, with the base annotated as it narrows. A wide triangular base would mean high fertility, a barrel a stationary population, and an urn that is top heavy a decline. India's outline keeps a still broad childhood trunk above a shrinking base, the look of fertility transition under way.
steps.say: Horizontal bars stacked by sex and by five year age groups draw India's 2011 population pyramid, with the base annotated as it narrows. A wide triangular base would mean high fertility, a barrel a stationary population, and an urn that is top heavy a decline. India's outline keeps a still broad childhood trunk above a shrinking base, the look of fertility transition under way.

steps.title: Expansive versus constrictive pyramids
steps.tx: Textbooks contrast the **expansive pyramid of developing populations** (wide base, concave sides, pointed apex from high mortality) with the constrictive pyramid of ageing societies (base narrower than the middle, convex sides, blunt top). Developing country pyramids also show a youth bulge and a dented working age male side where migration removes men, both features visible in Gulf linked Indian states.
steps.say: Developing pyramids are wide based triangles. Ageing societies narrow at the base and bulge in the middle and top.

steps.title: Sex ratio read from the pyramid
steps.tx: Because boys slightly outnumber girls at birth (about one hundred five males per hundred females) but females survive better at older ages, the **sex structure across the pyramid** flips with height: male surplus at the base, near balance in middle ages, and female surplus among the elderly. A missing wedge of young adult males signals out migration, while missing girls at the base expose sex selective practices.
steps.say: More boys are born, yet more women survive to old age. Missing young women at the base reveal sex selection; missing men suggest migration.

steps.title: Life table survival behind the net rate
steps.tx: The survival column of a **life table in demography** converts a synthetic cohort of one hundred thousand births into survivors at each age under current mortality, supplying the survival weights that turn gross into net reproduction. Life expectancy at birth reads from the same table's person years column, which is why fertility and mortality statistics share one mathematical household in every demography examination.
steps.say: Life tables supply the survival weights for the net reproduction rate. The same table also yields life expectancy at birth.

steps.title: Eligible couples and couple protection rate
steps.tx: Programme managers track the **eligible couple** (a married woman aged fifteen to forty nine with her husband) as the unit of family planning work, conventionally about one hundred fifty to one hundred eighty per thousand population. The couple protection rate estimates the share protected by sterilisation, intrauterine devices, pills, and condoms combined, and the unmet need for contraception captures couples wanting to space or limit without using any method.
steps.say: Eligible couples are the family planning denominator, roughly one hundred sixty per thousand people. Couple protection rate merges all methods in use.

steps.title: Choosing between reproduction rates
steps.tx: An examination stem asking whether the population will replace itself wants the **net reproduction rate**, one mentioning daughters without mortality wants the gross rate, and one using all births per thousand mid year population wants the crude birth rate. Remember the ladder: total fertility counts children, gross counts daughters, net counts surviving daughters, each step narrower and more prognostic than the last.
steps.say: Children, daughters, surviving daughters: that ladder separates total fertility, gross, and net rates. Replacement questions always mean the net rate.
